$comment: Starling runtime protocol envelope, v1 (E17 design note section 2).
This is the single wire shape shared by every command and event of the
five runtime state machines (capture, jobs, context/mode, docs, delivery).
commands.schema.json and events.schema.json refine this envelope per
message type; this schema is the structural baseline every message must
satisfy first.
Versioning: v identifies the payload grammar. v=1 is the grammar defined
by commands.schema.json / events.schema.json. A receiver that cannot
parse v MUST NOT apply the payload; it replies with the event
runtime.nack {reason: "unsupported_version"} carrying corr = the id of
the rejected message, and otherwise ignores the message. For a v1 schema
validator any v != 1 is therefore a validation failure.
Ordering: seq is per-stream monotonic (strictly increasing). A stream is
the correlation channel named by corr; messages without corr belong to
the direction stream of the connection ("commands" for commands,
"events" for events). A receiver must reject a message whose seq is not
greater than the last seq seen on its stream: duplicates and reordering
are failures to be surfaced, not silently absorbed.
Correlation: corr names the stream a message belongs to (for example the
take id across a capture start/stop pair). A command that expects an
outcome event and the event that resolves it must carry the same corr.
payload is required on every message; commands/events with no fields
carry an empty object.
